I agree with you that if someone has spammed 20 different subs with advertising the chances are excellent that their next posting will also be spam. However, there is a small chance that the next posting won't be. There is, in fact, a small chance that the next posting will be a regular contribution to discussion. I would rather take the risk of more spam than ban someone from contributing to a sub before they've said anything one way or the other. This approach has an excellent and time-honoured pedigree: it's known as "innocent until proven guilty". By all means, ban them once they've broken the sub rules, but until they do break those rules, they should be treated as anyone else. People shouldn't be punished for a crime they haven't yet committed.

I do agree that we need to deal with accounts that post spam, but I feel that the correct way to handle the problem is at the site level, not at the sub level. If an account is discovered to be posting spam and nothing else, then it should first be warned, rather as Wikipedia warns its vandals, then, if a further problem arises, the account should be banned at the site level. Ideally, this process should be as transparent as possible and, as with Wikipedia, should allow for appeals.

The advantage of my approach is that it takes decision power on the banning of problem accounts out of the hands of individual moderators in individual subs, thus eliminating the possibility that moderators may pre-emptively ban people just because they don't like their comments in other subs, and makes the entire banning process a shared endeavour of the entire community. This makes sense: in the real world troublemakers are dealt with by society at large (through the legal system etc.), rather than by individuals, using a generally transparent system that seeks to avoid personal prejudices. I would hope for something similar here.

I suppose my underlying philosophy is that I want us here in Voat to be a single huge community, brought together by a set of common values, with many separate sub-communities each with their own interests. This is rather different from what Reddit has become - a vast and dislocated network of individual fiefdoms, some of which are periodically at war with each other, and none of which any longer contributes to the common values of the whole. I want a Voat that is both diverse and tolerant. Yes, we have our individual interests and intellectual and social positions, but we are united by a broader commitment to free speech and multiple opinions, honestly stated and respectfully debated. Whilst we will always be vigilant against those who seek to curtail our freedom of expression, we can, and must, build a culture of open-ness and shared endeavour. It is by doing this that we will mark ourselves out as different from all the other sites, and it is by doing this that we will build a greater Voat.
